reader.requirement: At 1985 the file control entry of a sequential file accepts RECORD DELIMITER [IS] followed by exactly one of STANDARD-1 or an implementor-name, and refuses any other shape (no operand, two operands, a literal, the clause without RECORD, a word that is no implementor-name).

edition-consulted.switches: only the citation text inside the COBOL7598 and COBOL7599 messages (1985 locator at --std 85)
DELIMITER and STANDARD-1 reserved at every edition (all four columns true)

reader.edition-search: grep of src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Editions and constructs/ for record.?delimiter, STANDARD-1, DELIMITER: no ConstructRegistry row, no version predicate in the grammar rule; the binder arm is edition-invariant except EditionContext.Cite text.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise both arms with and without IS and a non-name word; the parse refusals of degenerate forms (no operand, two operands, a literal, DELIMITER without RECORD) are not exercised

reader.notes: The grammar rule is the format verbatim (RECORD DELIMITER IS? (STANDARD_1 | cobolWord)) and the binder narrows cobolWord to the implementor-name table (BINARY-SEQUENTIAL, LINE-SEQUENTIAL). The general-format diagram itself is not quotable by cite.py (box-drawn), so the clause's function and rules are cited. Minor: the COBOL1778 and COBOL1970 messages cite §2023 even at --std 85; not part of this rule.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VII.2.8 whole and the grammar rule recordDelimiterClause (RECORD DELIMITER IS? (STANDARD_1 | cobolWord)) with FileControlBinder.BindFileControl/ApplyRecordDelimiter/ScreenRecordDelimiter. Attacked the format's placement (the clause belongs to the Sequential I-O file control entry only) and degenerate shapes the reader did not try, at --std 85: rdA RELATIVE + RECORD DELIMITER -> COBOL2912 refused; rdB INDEXED + RECORD DELIMITER -> COBOL2912 refused; rdC sort file (SD) + RECORD DELIMITER -> COBOL1900 citing §1985:XI.2.3.3 SR2; rdD the clause written twice -> COBOL2423; rdF RECORD DELIMITER IS STANDARD-2 (a reserved word that is no implementor-name) -> COBOL5506; rdE lower-case 'record delimiter line-sequential' (IS omitted) on RECORD CONTAINS 1 TO 8 -> compiles and runs, records read back [ABC     ] [ABCDEFGH]. Every shape the format refuses is refused and every shape it admits is accepted. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.2.8.3 SR1  the text is in SR1'; 'OK  §1985:XI.2.3.3 SR2  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR3  the text is in GR3'. Wording only: COBOL2912/COBOL2423/COBOL5506 cite §2023 at --std 85.
